title: Exact triple response laws and site-size counts fixed site groups in 615 selected worm circuit models
abstract: We tested whether exact three-target response laws identify shared synaptic-site groups when the number of sites at each size is known. We used 615 selected source circuits with three through eight retained targets from eight C. elegans brain maps. Equal independent Bernoulli release and unit shared effects turn response laws into target intersection counts. Exact triple constraints fixed every site-group multiset: 614 circuits had full column rank and one had an exact nonnegative-solution certificate. Independent checks confirmed all certificates. Pair laws left five circuits with exact alternatives. For these five examples, a model-only silence test gave sufficient trial bounds from 637 to 7,144 at release probability 0.2 and from 819 to 439,722 at probability 0.5. A synthetic fixed-size trade shows that triple laws do not suffice in all circuits. This is a conditional identification result, not measured neural noise. Selected small circuits, partial maps, unknown release laws and exact-count assumptions limit transfer. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External synapse records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Pair laws left five selected circuits with alternative site groups. Triple laws and site-size counts fixed every selected grouping under the stated model.
